Calibrate the IDS Cutoff on Control Samples

Source: R/module_uncertainty.R
CalibrateIDS.Rd

Derives a cohort-specific IDS cutoff from control samples of the same tissue, platform and preprocessing, and expresses each sample's IDS relative to the control distribution. The package default cutoff (0.2) is exploratory; control IDS depends on tissue and sample type, so a cutoff calibrated on matched controls is preferable when such controls exist.

Usage

CalibrateIDS(
  results,
  controls,
  method = c("quantile", "max", "youden"),
  probs = 0.99,
  cases = NULL
)

Arguments

results

A data frame returned by AnalyzeImprintStatus() (for example results(x)[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected"]]), with columns Sample_Name and IDS.

controls

Control samples: Sample_Group value(s), sample names, or a logical vector along the rows of results.

method

How the cutoff is derived:

  • "quantile" (default): the probs quantile of control IDS;

  • "max": the maximum control IDS;

  • "youden": the cutoff maximizing sensitivity + specificity between cases and controls (requires cases). Candidate cutoffs lie midway between adjacent observed IDS values; among tied optima the middle one is taken.

probs

Quantile used by method = "quantile" (default 0.99).

cases

Optional case samples, given like controls. Required for "youden"; when given, the area under the ROC curve (cases versus controls) is reported.

Value

results with added columns IDS_z (robust z-score, (IDS - median) / MAD of the controls, with the MAD floored at 0.01), IDS_control_percentile (percentage of controls with a lower or equal IDS) and Status_calibrated ("Imprinting Alteration" when IDS > cutoff, otherwise "Normal"; for "youden", IDS >= cutoff). The attribute calibration is a one-row data frame with the method, cutoff, number of controls, control median and maximum IDS, and the AUC and Youden sensitivity/specificity when cases are given.

Details

Control IDS should come from the same scoring run as the cases. With a control reference (reference_group or reference_samples in AnalyzeImprintStatus()) each control is scored leave-one-out, so its IDS is an honest estimate of control variation; with the fixed 0.5 reference the control IDS measures the controls' offset from 0.5.

Examples

res <- data.frame(Sample_Name = paste0("S", 1:8),
                  Sample_Group = rep(c("control", "case"), each = 4),
                  IDS = c(0.03, 0.05, 0.04, 0.08, 0.30, 0.12, 0.45, 0.26))
cal <- CalibrateIDS(res, controls = "control", method = "max", cases = "case")
#> Warning: Calibration on 4 controls; at least 5 tissue-matched controls are recommended.
attr(cal, "calibration")
#>   method probs cutoff n_controls control_median control_max n_cases AUC
#> 1    max    NA   0.08          4          0.045        0.08       4   1
#>   sensitivity specificity
#> 1           1           1
